name: Double-Orifice Mitral Valve

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Double-Orifice Mitral Valve

criteria.description: Visualization of two distinct mitral valve orifices on echocardiography
Assessment of mitral valve function showing regurgitation or stenosis associated with double orifice
Presence of associated congenital cardiac anomalies such as atrioventricular septal defect

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Visualization of two distinct mitral valve orifices on echocardiography with assessment of valve function
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on echocardiographic imaging; cardiac MRI may be used for further anatomical delineation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bifid mitral valve orifice detected by echocardiography
searchTerms: bifid valve seen on heart ultrasound

pathognomonic.symptomName: Mitral valve regurgitation due to double orifice
searchTerms: mitral valve leaking due to double opening

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to decreased cardiac output
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output

common.symptomName: Murmur consistent with mitral valve abnormality
searchTerms: heart murmur from mitral valve problem
abnormal heart sounds at mitral valve

common.notes: Due to arrhythmias secondary to valve dysfunction

occasional.symptomName: Chest discomfort or atypical chest pain
searchTerms: chest discomfort or unusual chest pain

occasional.notes: Due to congestive heart failure in advanced cases
Secondary to arrhythmia or low cardiac output

rare.symptomName: Infective endocarditis involving the mitral valve
Stroke due to embolism from mitral valve abnormality
searchTerms: stroke caused by mitral valve embolism
brain infarct from heart valve clot

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension secondary to mitral valve dysfunction
searchTerms: high blood pressure in lungs from mitral valve
pulmonary hypertension due to valve dysfunction
lung artery pressure increase secondary to mitral valve

laboratory: Generally normal; may show elevated BNP in heart failure
Blood cultures if infective endocarditis suspected
imaging: Echocardiography showing two mitral valve orifices
Doppler studies demonstrating mitral regurgitation or stenosis
Cardiac MRI for detailed anatomical assessment
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be sporadic or associated with congenital heart disease syndromes
other: Electrocardiogram may show arrhythmias or left atrial enlargement

distinguishingFeatures: Single mitral valve orifice with leaflet prolapse
Single mitral orifice with chordae tendineae attached to a single papillary muscle

redFlags: Severe mitral regurgitation causing heart failure
Sudden onset of stroke or embolic events
references: Ghahremani GG, et al. Double-orifice mitral valve: radiologic-pathologic correlation. Radiographics. 1992.
Mavroudis C, Backer CL. Pediatric Cardiac Surgery. 4th ed. 2013.
